Guides

Short notes on making markers that read, and on why the Studio works the way it does. Each number comes from the Studio's own core.

Where to put a label, and a corner markA short id on the black border row at the Studio's size, or outside the quiet zone; never in it. Measured by Verify on a test board you can open.Profile firstPick a profile like an extrude; the marker goes in its largest clear box. Draw a rectangle to place it exactly.Exact sizes, and the size stepTyped sizes are exact; driven ones round to 0.5 mm, a step you set, or whole printer dots.Heights for 3D printingInkjet has the paper; 3D print has a white and a black height, the black from the white's outer face.Trim: profile or markerThe sticker is cut to the whole profile, or just the marker and its quiet zone.Marker ids: next, and Re-IDNew markers take the next free id, typed ids win, given ids never move; Re-ID renumbers in board order.

Every number on these pages is computed by ArUco Studio's own core, the same Python that runs in the Studio: docs/build_guides.py runs it and writes the pages.
